_sample_note: Sample 01 (reference suite): one dataflow group exercising every merge-style CDC strategy side by side, all assets isolated in the {{catalog}}.metaflow_sample schema. Three CDC ingestion flows (SCD1 customers, SCD2 suppliers, FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC parts) plus one APPEND order-events ingestion flow whose only job is to give the SCD3 transformation a legally streamable upstream: every merge-CDC target (SCD1/SCD2/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC) is written via dlt.apply_changes[_from_snapshot] and therefore can NEVER be read as a stream (DELTA_SOURCE_TABLE_IGNORE_CHANGES), while dlt.apply_changes for the SCD3 pivot REQUIRES a streaming source -- so the SCD3 flow joins the streaming APPEND order-events table (stream side) to the SCD1 customer dimension (static batch side, a legal stream-static inner join over two tables this same pipeline publishes). The seed notebook (notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/04_seed_sample_01_multi_scd_data.py) lands 3 iterations of DISTINCT data: iteration 2 mutates values for existing SCD1/SCD2 keys (in-place overwrite vs. new history version), iteration 3 adds new keys and further changes, and each iteration advances every order through OPENED -> PROCESSING -> FULFILLED so the SCD3 current/previous pivot is visible. HARD CONSTRAINT observed from live testing: apply_changes_from_snapshot reads its snapshot-input dataset's CURRENT CONTENTS, which ACCUMULATE over a streaming Auto Loader upstream -- so the FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC parts feed is strictly ADDITIVE across iterations (new part keys only, never a changed or removed existing key: a changed key would appear twice in one accumulated snapshot, a removed key would never be deleted).

ingestion_flows.source_description: Sample 01: SCD1 customer dimension from samples.tpch.customer slices. Iteration 1 lands the base dimension, iteration 2 re-lands changed customers (segment/balance updates overwrite in place, no history), iteration 3 adds brand-new customer keys plus further balance changes.

Sample 01: SCD2 supplier dimension from samples.tpch.supplier slices. columns_to_check scopes history tracking to account_balance/nation_key -- iteration 2's balance changes open new __START_AT/__END_AT versions instead of overwriting, iteration 3 adds new supplier keys and moves some suppliers to a new nation.

Sample 01: FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC part feed from samples.tpch.part slices, diffed by apply_changes_from_snapshot on part_id. STRICTLY ADDITIVE across the 3 iterations (iteration 1: keys 1-40, iteration 2: keys 41-60, iteration 3: keys 61-80; never a changed or removed existing key) -- the snapshot-input dataset accumulates over a streaming Auto Loader upstream, so multi-snapshot diffing cannot delete removed keys and a re-landed existing key would appear twice in one snapshot. See this spec's _sample_note.

Sample 01: APPEND order-event feed from samples.tpch.orders slices -- the append-only, legally-streamable upstream the SCD3 transformation flow requires (every merge-CDC target in this group is apply_changes-written and cannot be streamed). Each iteration advances the SAME 20 order keys one status step (OPENED -> PROCESSING -> FULFILLED) so the SCD3 current/previous pivot is observable.

transformation_flows.source_description: Sample 01: SCD3 current/previous order-status pivot over a stream-static inner join of two tables this same pipeline publishes -- the streaming APPEND order-events table (stream side) enriched with the SCD1 customer dimension (static batch side). columns_to_check scopes the pivot to order_status, so after iteration 3 every order shows current_order_status FULFILLED / previous_order_status PROCESSING.
transformation_flows.transformation_sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, c.customer_name, c.market_segment, o.order_status, o.total_price, o.event_ts FROM sample01_order_events_src o INNER JOIN sample01_customer_dim_src c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
